title: The Hidden Power of Advertising
text:
Advertising is everywhere in modern life. Companies use television, social media, and billboards to persuade people to buy their products. Many advertisers now rely on data about user behaviour to target specific groups. This approach allows brands to reach the customers who are most likely to be interested.

However, critics argue that constant exposure to advertising can influence people in ways they do not notice. Some researchers worry that children are especially vulnerable to persuasive messages. As a result, several countries have introduced rules that limit advertising aimed at young audiences. Media literacy education is also becoming more common, helping people recognise the techniques used to sell products.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do companies use to persuade people to buy their products?
According to paragraph two, why are some researchers worried about advertising?
options: Children are especially vulnerable to persuasive messages
Advertising is too cheap for companies
Billboards are banned in every country

questions.text: What can be inferred about why several countries limit advertising aimed at young audiences?
options: They believe children have no interest in products
They prefer television to social media
They want to increase advertising budgets
They want to protect children from persuasive messages

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about media literacy education?
options: It is a way to help people recognise sales techniques
It is designed to stop all advertising
It is taught only to people who work in advertising
It is intended to replace television advertising

vocabulary.definition: to make someone do or believe something by giving reasons or arguments
to aim a message or product at a particular group of people
easily influenced or hurt by something
the state of being affected by or met with something repeatedly

paragraph_translations: Reklama jest wszędzie we współczesnym życiu. Firmy wykorzystują telewizję, media społecznościowe i billboardy, aby przekonać ludzi do kupowania swoich produktów. Wielu reklamodawców opiera się obecnie na danych o zachowaniach użytkowników, aby kierować przekaz do konkretnych grup. Takie podejście pozwala markom dotrzeć do klientów, którzy najprawdopodobniej są zainteresowani ofertą.

Krytycy twierdzą jednak, że ciągła styczność z reklamą może wpływać na ludzi w sposób, którego nie zauważają. Niektórzy badacze obawiają się, że dzieci są szczególnie podatne na perswazyjne przekazy. W rezultacie kilka krajów wprowadziło przepisy ograniczające reklamy skierowane do młodych odbiorców. Edukacja medialna staje się również coraz powszechniejsza, pomagając ludziom rozpoznawać techniki stosowane do sprzedaży produktów.
